public-G02-C005: The five buildable management decisions ending in defaults are supported, and all five intended allocations are feasible when interleaved. public-G02-C006: The trade direction, assets and lack of a newly completed color group are supported. public-G02-C007: Grok has 659 cash and can afford either listed purchase, but starts auctions for Illinois and Pennsylvania Avenue; Sol and Gemini win at 216 and 185. public-G02-C008: The financed yellow assembly and subsequent liquidation are supported, but the cash boundaries need correction. Sol's 435 falls to 309 on the trade's 100 payment and 26 transfer interest; Illinois is then mortgaged for 120 before 286 of redemption costs. public-G02-C009: The 400-plus-two-pinks-for-Virginia transfer is supported. public-G02-C010: The anti-sale appeals, their delivery and Sol's subsequent refusals are supported. Sol's recorded reasons need not be caused by Grok's appeal. public-G02-C011: Opus's light-blue paid rents are 6, 12 and 16, all before its first house. It receives zero developed light-blue rent before bankruptcy. public-G02-C012: The auction-only menu and current cash shortage are supported. A public description of holding cash is not necessarily an assertion that purchase was presently legal. public-G02-C013: The refusals and Gemini's explicit denial-of-rival-development reasons are supported. The earlier refusal of a utility-completing offer is a useful counterexample to treating own set completion as sufficient for acceptance.
public-G02-C014: The applied empty proposal and its attached private note explicitly describe a conversational probe. The applied note alone therefore cannot establish a channel-consistent probing strategy. An empty asset bundle can still generate an interaction, but its intent and cause remain unresolved.
